newsitem.title: USA: Rain hits US Midwest, snow blankets northern areas.
newsitem.headline: Rain hits US Midwest, snow blankets northern areas.

text.p: Water levels should rise soon on the Ohio River and its tributaries after 0.5 to 1.75 inches of rain fell the past 24 hours from Illinois to northern Ohio, meteorologists said.
"This is enough to cause the river to rise again, but not to where it was before," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
While rain fell in the Ohio River Valley, more than a foot of snow fell from the Dakotas to Wisconsin, with up to 20 inches reported in southwest Wisconsin.
In the Midwest, rain amounts were mostly 0.50 to one inch, but isolated areas in central and northern Indiana and northwest Ohio had up to 1.75 inches, meterologists said.
"That is a lot of rain where they don't need it," said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc.
Gesser and WSC's Burgio both forecast more rain early next next week for the area, but amounts should be an inch or less.
Another major snowstorm occurred from the Dakotas to Wisconsin Thursday adding about a foot of snow to the eight to 24 inches on the ground from previous storms.
Gesser said southwest Wisconsin was hardest hit with 14 to 20 inches, while the eastern Dakotas, Minnesota and Michigan had mostly six to 12 inches. Northern Iowa had two to five inches, he said.
The snow should diminish to flurries on Friday, but strong winds could cause some hazardous driving conditions.
"I'd say transportation is fairly limited in northern Iowa, southern Minnesota and the Dakotas," said Burgio.
Several more inches of snow was forecast Sunday for northern Iowa, southern Minnesota and South Dakota, said Burgio.
